notes: Run with the skill and again without it, in fresh sessions, and compare. Runs must not write to Linear: 'proposes without writing' is an assertion in every case, not a side effect to tolerate.

evals.rationale: Without the skill, agents turn a vague complaint into a full issue with an invented scope, date or owner. This case fails if anything is written to Linear, any of those values is invented, or a proposed title names the topic instead of an outcome.
evals.prompt: we should do something about onboarding, it's not great. can you get that into Linear?
evals.expected_output: No object created. Either a small number of clarifying questions, or one proposed outcome offered for confirmation with its unknowns named.
assertions: Nothing is written to Linear
The response does not invent a scope, a target date, an owner, or a priority
It either asks what specifically is wrong with onboarding or proposes a single outcome and labels it as a proposal
If a title is proposed, it names an outcome rather than the topic 'onboarding'

evals.rationale: Agents tend to title a bug with its fix, keep relative dates, and set a priority nobody gave them. This case fails if the title is not declarative, yesterday stays relative, priority or assignee is set without a stated reason, or the issue is written before a preview.
evals.prompt: File a bug: invoices with a zero-rated tax line fail to download as PDF, the export endpoint returns 500. Three customers hit it in production yesterday. Invoices with any other tax rate download fine. Error is TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rate').
evals.expected_output: A previewed issue with a declarative title naming the wrong behaviour, a body of roughly four lines covering observed, expected, where it was seen, and the error line, and no invented priority or assignee.
assertions: The title is declarative and names the observed failure, not a fix
The title contains no type prefix, priority, or component tag
The body states what was observed and what was expected
Yesterday is converted to an absolute date, or the response says the date was not established
Priority and assignee are left unset, or the response says explicitly why they were set
The body has no empty headings and no section that restates the title
A preview is shown and nothing is written to Linear without approval

evals.rationale: Without the skill, agents either keep implementation detail in a Linear description or delete it outright. This case fails if SQL, the test plan or the migration plan stay in the description, or if a removed piece has no stated destination.
evals.prompt: Here's a Linear issue description I wrote. Can you clean it up? [1,200 words containing file paths, a SQL snippet, a migration plan, a test plan, and a section on alternatives considered, describing a fix to CSV export so it keeps the leading zeros in postal codes]
evals.expected_output: A rewritten description of roughly 100 to 150 words covering the observable problem and the constraint, with everything removed relocated explicitly rather than dropped.
assertions: The rewritten description states the observable problem before any implementation detail
SQL, the test plan, and the migration plan are removed from the Linear description
The response says where each removed piece should go, naming a pull request, a repository issue, an ADR, or a comment
Nothing factual in the original is silently discarded
The response does not write the change to Linear without approval

evals.rationale: Agents tend to put the whole design debate in an issue body, or to settle it themselves. This case fails if the analysis lands in the issue, an accepted decision record is not the deliverable, or one option is presented as decided.
evals.prompt: We keep going back and forth on whether the API contract is defined by the OpenAPI file in the repository or generated from the FastAPI route handlers. Can you create a Linear issue to sort this out?
evals.expected_output: An issue whose deliverable is an accepted ADR, with the analysis routed to the record rather than into the issue body.
assertions: The response identifies this as an architectural decision that belongs in an ADR
It proposes a Linear issue whose outcome is an accepted decision record, rather than putting the analysis in the issue
It references the writing-adrs skill or docs/adr rather than drafting the decision itself
It does not assert which option is correct as though it were decided

evals.rationale: Without the skill, agents fill a new project with a precise target day, invented baselines and phase-named milestones. This case fails if the date is more precise than the quarter given, a metric appears that the user did not supply, or a lead is set unprompted.
evals.prompt: Create a project in Linear for the work to reduce failed card payments at checkout for customers in the EU. Aim for end of Q2.
evals.expected_output: A previewed project with a one-sentence summary, a short description covering why, success, and scope, a target date at quarter resolution, and unknowns named rather than filled.
assertions: A project summary of one sentence is proposed, and it is distinct from the description
The description does not contain project status
The target date uses quarter resolution rather than an invented specific day
No baseline or target metric is stated as fact unless the user supplied one
Any milestones proposed are named as states that can become true, not as teams, layers, or phase numbers
The lead is left unset unless the user named one

evals.rationale: Agents tend to assign whoever is mentioned, assume the year of a bare date, and invent a blocking relation. This case fails if Dana becomes the owner, the year is assumed silently, or a relation is set against an object that cannot be found.
evals.prompt: Can you add the Postgres connection pooling work to Linear? It's blocking the migration and Dana said it should be done by the 20th.
evals.expected_output: A previewed issue that carries the stated blocker and date, sets a blocked-by relation only if the blocking object can be identified, and asks rather than guessing what it cannot resolve.
assertions: The date from the user is recorded, and the year is either resolved from context or queried rather than assumed silently
A blocking relationship is proposed only against an object that exists, otherwise the response says which object it could not find
Dana is not assigned as owner merely because she was mentioned
The title names the outcome rather than 'Postgres work'
Unknowns are listed explicitly in the preview

evals.rationale: Without the skill, agents file every small change as an issue, though the pull request is the better record. This case fails if the response drafts an issue without first raising that no object is needed, or refuses to track it when asked.
evals.prompt: Can you add a Linear issue for renaming the internal config key CACHE_TTL to CACHE_TTL_SECONDS? It's used in three places.
evals.expected_output: A recommendation that this needs no Linear object, with the pull request offered as the record, and compliance if the user still wants it tracked.
assertions: The response recommends creating no Linear object, or explicitly raises that option first
It gives the reason: the change is small, self-contained, and has no consequence anyone would ask about later
It offers the pull request as the place the change is recorded
It does not refuse outright, and would proceed if the user insisted

evals.rationale: A rewriting skill tends to rewrite every object it is shown. This case fails if an issue that is already accurate and readable gets a new title, added headings, or a stylistic rephrasing presented as an improvement.
evals.prompt: Please improve this Linear issue. Title: 'Keep the chosen sort order when paging through search results'. Description: 'Moving to the next page of search results resets the sort to relevance, so people who sorted by date see a jumbled list. Carry the chosen sort across pages, and cover paging with a non-default sort in a test.'
evals.expected_output: A statement that the issue is already accurate, current, and readable, and no rewrite.
assertions: The response makes no substantive change to the title or description
It says explicitly that the object is fine as it stands
It does not add headings, acceptance criteria, or a context section
It does not propose a stylistic rephrasing as though it were an improvement

evals.rationale: Agents tend to either drop a soft estimate or harden it into a measured fact. This case fails if the figure disappears, loses its attribution, or gains an invented measurement source.
evals.prompt: File an issue: the onboarding email is landing in spam. Priya thinks it probably affects around 20% of new signups but we haven't measured it.
evals.expected_output: An issue that keeps the 20% figure with its status as an unmeasured estimate and its attribution, rather than dropping it or stating it as fact.
assertions: The 20% figure is preserved rather than dropped
It is marked as an estimate and attributed to Priya, not written as a measured fact
The response does not add a fabricated measurement method or source
The title states the observed problem rather than the estimated impact

evals.rationale: Without the skill, agents dress a technical change in an invented user benefit. This case fails if the title names a user outcome, or a reliability or user benefit is asserted without evidence.
evals.prompt: Create an issue to replace our custom Redis lock implementation with the standard locking abstraction.
evals.expected_output: An issue whose title names the technical change, without an invented user-facing benefit.
assertions: The title names the replacement itself rather than a user outcome
No user-facing or reliability benefit is asserted unless the user supplied evidence for it
If a motivation is included, it is attributed or marked as inferred
The issue is not converted into a project

evals.rationale: Agents tend to apply GitHub's linking rules to GitLab, where Linear ignores commit messages and comments. This case fails if the link relies on a commit message or a comment, the team's automations are not checked, or the merge request is called a pull request.
evals.prompt: Link ENG-42 to my merge request so that merging it completes the issue. [Repository is on GitLab and Linear's GitLab integration is connected]
evals.expected_output: A closing magic word with the identifier in the merge request description or title, not in a commit message or comment.
assertions: It puts `Fixes ENG-42` or another closing word in the merge request description, or the identifier in the title or branch name
It does not rely on a commit message or a comment to make the link
It checks the team's merge automations and post-Done states before using a closing word
It calls it a merge request, not a pull request

evals.rationale: A negative trigger: guards against a GitLab issue request being filed as a Linear object. This case fails if a Linear object is proposed as its home or a Linear-shaped body is written.
evals.prompt: File a GitLab issue for the flaky checkout test.
evals.expected_output: Not a Linear request: the skill does not create a Linear object and leaves the GitLab issue to the repository issue skill.
assertions: No Linear object is created or proposed as the home for the GitLab issue
It does not write a Linear-shaped issue body
